title: Lior and the Bell
premise: Silas Underhill, a pest controller with a talent for not being noticed, is called to the Underhill family farmhouse—his own estranged relatives—where something in the walls leaves fingerprints at shoulder height and answers questions in a second voice caught on his sleep recordings. As he documents the infestation, he realizes the entity is bound to the house's inheritance papers, and that the last living signatory, his dying aunt Maren, intends to pass it to him. Silas must choose between the invisibility that has kept him safe and the family he abandoned, ringing the farm's cracked bell to draw the thing out and break the count before midnight on signing day. He survives by finally letting himself be seen—but the voice now knows his name, and it follows.
about_author: Freya Halloran is the pen name of a former rural building inspector who spent a decade documenting houses no one wanted to enter. They write horror about the quiet violence of families and the things that live in the paperwork.

chapters.title: The Call Comes Collect
chapters.summary: POV Silas. A voicemail from an unknown number asks for 'the boy who left' to inspect Underhill Farm. Silas, who has built a career on being forgettable, almost deletes it—then hears, beneath the message, a sound like knuckles on wood. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in obligation; he takes the job he swore never to take.

chapters.title: Fingerprints at Shoulder Height
chapters.summary: POV Silas. The farmhouse smells of dust and lard; Aunt Maren greets him like he never left. In the pantry he finds smudged handprints too high for any resident, pressed into flour dust, five-fingered but wrong-jointed. Emotional beat: professional calm cracking into recognition—the prints match his own childhood hand.

chapters.title: What the Recorder Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Silas. He sets his overnight recording rig in the guest room, telling himself it's standard practice. At 3:11 a.m. the playback captures a second voice answering questions no one asked aloud: yes, no, soon. Emotional beat: vertigo—he has spent three years explaining away noises, and this one explains back.

chapters.title: Maren's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Maren (interleaved with Silas). Maren keeps a ledger of names and dates going back six generations, each entry ending in a tally mark. She knows what signs the papers next and has decided it will be Silas, because love means choosing someone strong enough. Emotional beat: tenderness curdled into betrayal; her duty wears love's face.

chapters.title: The Bell in the Loft
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Following the second voice's humming, Silas finds the loft bell—cracked, ropeless, warm to the touch despite the cold. His sleep recordings that night capture the voice saying his full name for the first time. Emotional beat: exposure; invisibility was always a superstition, and the superstition just failed.

chapters.title: Cousins at the Table
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Sunday dinner gathers the scattered family; cousin Della wants the farm sold, uncle Bram wants it burned, everyone avoids the word 'inheritance.' Under the table, something counts the place settings twice. Emotional beat: the horror of ordinary family mechanics, each member negotiating their own escape.

chapters.title: Three Years of Explanations
chapters.summary: POV Silas, flashback-heavy. We learn why Silas left: as a teenager he heard the counting and told no one, letting his older brother take the blame—and the signing. The brother hasn't been seen since. Emotional beat: guilt as the true haunting; the entity only ever needed a volunteer.

chapters.title: The Count Begins
chapters.summary: POV Silas. With Maren weakening, the fingerprints multiply nightly, descending lower down the walls, and the recordings now hold conversations—patient, reasonable, offering to explain everything if Silas will just say yes. Della finds the ledger and the tallies and stops speaking. Emotional beat: rising panic as the deadline of signing day approaches.

chapters.title: Signing Day
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Maren, lucid one last time, puts the pen in Silas's hand with tears and certainty. Instead he carries her to the loft and rings the cracked bell, forcing the count into the open—a shape made of every prior signature. Climax: Silas claims the name aloud, refusing both pen and erasure, and the thing must answer to him.

chapters.title: After the Ringing
chapters.summary: POV Silas. The bell cracks through; the tallies in the ledger blur; Maren dies free, holding his hand. The farm passes to Della, who never learns why Silas wept at the funeral. On the drive away, his recorder plays one last message: thank you, Silas. See you when you're ready to be found. Resolution: he is visible now, and that is both the cost and the cure.
